## 2026 {#year-2026}

::: {.news-entry}
### PhD recruitment under way {#phd-recruitment-update}

[September 2026]{.news-date}

The application period for the PhD position in the project *Enabling flexible hydropower operation by
AI-based active flow control* closed on 31 August 2026, and the assessment and recruitment process has
now started.

We received a large number of applications, so the process will take some time. Thank you to all
applicants for your patience. The position is expected to start in autumn 2026.

Read more about the research on the [project page](project-hydropower-ai.qmd).
:::

::: {.news-entry}
### Review paper on PINNs for the lid-driven cavity problem {#pinn-cavity-review}

[August 2026]{.news-date}

Our paper *State-of-the-art implementations of PINNs for the lid-driven cavity problem – a critical
review with future perspectives* is published in *Results in Engineering* (vol. 32, 112399).

Authors: M. Sheikholeslami, S. Salehi, W. Mao, A. Eslamdoost and H. Nilsson. The work is part of
Mohammad Sheikholeslami's PhD project on multi-fidelity physics-informed neural networks at Chalmers
University of Technology, which I co-supervise. See also the [PINN research theme](research.qmd#pinns).

[Read the paper (DOI: 10.1016/j.rineng.2026.112399)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rineng.2026.112399)
:::

::: {.news-entry}
### Talk and session chair at the 21st OpenFOAM Workshop {#ofw21}

[July 2026]{.news-date}

At the 21st OpenFOAM Workshop (OFW21) in Guimarães, Portugal, I presented *Closed-loop control of vortex
rope in a swirl generator using deep reinforcement learning* and chaired the Multiphase Flows I session.

A swirl generator is a simplified model of the flow in a hydraulic turbine draft tube. For background,
see the [flow control research theme](research.qmd#flow-control).
:::

::: {.news-entry}
### Section Editor of the OpenFOAM Journal {#ofj-section-editor}

[June 2026]{.news-date}

I have joined the editorial team of the [OpenFOAM Journal](https://journal.openfoam.com/index.php/ofj/about/editorialTeam)
as Section Editor. I also serve on the OpenFOAM Turbomachinery Technical Committee within the
[OpenFOAM Governance](https://www.openfoam.com/governance/overview).
:::

::: {.news-entry}
### New PhD position in AI-based flow control for hydropower {#phd-position}

[June 2026]{.news-date}

A PhD position was advertised in the project *Enabling flexible hydropower operation by AI-based active
flow control*, funded by an ÅForsk Foundation Early-Career Research Grant with co-funding from Linköping
University. The project couples deep reinforcement learning with high-fidelity CFD to suppress harmful
flow instabilities in hydraulic turbines.

The student will be based at Linköping University, with Håkan Nilsson (Chalmers University of
Technology) as co-supervisor. The application deadline was 31 August 2026.

[About the project](project-hydropower-ai.qmd)
:::

## 2025 {#year-2025}

::: {.news-entry}
### Review paper on the lifetime of hydro turbines {#lifetime-review}

[December 2025]{.news-date}

Our review *Lifetime analysis of hydro turbines with focus on fatigue damage in a renewable energy
system* is published in *Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews* (vol. 228, 116578).

Authors: M. Nobilo, S. Salehi and H. Nilsson. The paper reviews how transient and off-design operation,
increasingly common as hydropower balances wind and solar power, affects fatigue damage and lifetime of
hydro turbines. It is part of Martina Nobilo's doctoral work at Chalmers University of Technology, which
I co-supervised. See also the [flexible hydropower research theme](research.qmd#hydropower).

[Read the paper (DOI: 10.1016/j.rser.2025.116578)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2025.116578)
:::

### Joined Linköping University {#joined-liu}

[August 2025]{.news-date}

I joined Linköping University as Associate Professor of Fluid Mechanics in the Division of Applied
